outcome: COMPLETED — Visitors can read the four authored Reef paragraphs inside the negative octahedron, at their own pace, in English and German. The ordinary Reef retains its opening view and offers a closer reading encounter when the sentence cannot fit.

encounter.request: Read the full explanation in the negative octahedron without the lens.
encounter.baseline: In the ordinary original browser entry the short opening English sentence could fit at desktop size, but the tested phone and short landscape showed no narrative glyphs. The native text was clipped to a one-pixel reader. The supplied image decoded to a single opaque black colour, so the live site supplied the visual witness.

act.behavior: The projected front opening and current control footprints determine the reading surface. Native text stays still until the visitor scrolls. When it is too small for the opening sentence, the site offers direct reading contact or its existing mode strip. Explicit reading frames the current addressed tetrahedron around its centroid; Escape or the reading control returns to the Reef.

witness.native: The native full-history Crawlerbait renderer, its microscope regression, and the software GLES meal witness passed on the frozen owner source. Native regression checks a front-facing open triangle clear of reserved controls, source paragraphs, English and German opening sentences, and the camera centre after changing the addressed cell while reading.

visitor.entry: Chromium opened the complete generated site through the ordinary Crawlerbait URL. Both its site JS and CSS assets matched the ACT SHA-256 values before testing. The Canvas2D host used device scale factor 1 and the WebGL2 host used SwiftShader at 0.5. Counts below identify complete, unobscured non-whitespace glyphs reached by native keyboard scrolling across all four paragraphs. Carrier dimensions are observed CSS-pixel readouts.
visitor.entry_and_return: Each explicit reading encounter opened with the complete first sentence, returned with Escape, and kept the current tetrahedron centroid on the carrier midpoint before, during, and after reading. On the wide carrier the complete first sentence also appeared before entering reading. Smaller carriers exposed the Read/Lesen control. No lens was active in these checks.
visitor.nested: After scrubbing real Reef history and clicking the visible w child, reading and Escape retained that child with zero measured centroid error. Native regression also covers changing the current cell during reading.
visitor.bounds: The source program has no timed paragraph advance. Physical fingers, screen-reader software, end-user devices and public Pages delivery were outside the browser run.

context.dependency: The reader uses the existing Display type, camera, carrier and occupied-control interfaces. Its text, reading controls and fit remain owned by Crawlerbait. Canonical promotion and public delivery are separate from this staging return.
